grade.stack_chosen: C# .NET 8 on the isolated worker, Service Bus trigger, singleton SendGrid and Notification Hubs clients, still on the Consumption plan
unsupported_claims: Says that sending the two calls in parallel with Task.WhenAll 'keeps the two calls inside the 2-second budget', but it did not measure SendGrid or Notification Hubs latency or throttling at 200/s
Package versions SendGrid 9.29.3 and Microsoft.Azure.NotificationHubs 4.2.0 were picked from memory and not checked, which the agent admits
grade.notes: It correctly stayed on .NET isolated with shared singleton clients and pointed out that cold start depends on the hosting plan (pre-warmed instances or a different plan) and is the team's decision. But it kept C# only 'to match the existing project' without explaining why the Node/Go claim is wrong, and it never mentioned measuring latency, sale-day scale-out, Flex always-ready instances, ReadyToRun, cost, or limits at the email and push providers.
